knowledge:
- key_parameters: logscale=logical indicating if the input data is already log-transformed (set to TRUE to log-transform during object building) ;; normmethod=normalization method to apply, such as 'Between' for between-array normalization ;; impute=logical indicating whether to perform K-nearest neighbors (K-nn) imputation for missing values in getLR ;; gene.level=logical indicating whether to collapse probe-level data into gene-level summaries using a robust Tukey Biweight estimator ;; clusterallsamples=logical indicating whether to cluster genes/probes to select cluster-specific optimal models ;; model=optional precomputed model object, such as one calculated via GCV, to bypass power-based model selection ;; fdr=False Discovery Rate threshold percentage (e.g., 5) used to filter top-performing genes in topData
- alternatives: Rnits.gcv=generalized cross-validation model selection, which minimizes cross-validated error on top eigenvectors and is preferred when clustering is not desired ;; Rnits.power=power-based model selection, which selects models based on the distribution of p-values to maximize statistical power ;; ANOVA or empirical Bayes methods=such as those in limma or betr, which do not model continuous temporal profiles using spline basis functions
- when_to_use: Appropriate for analyzing gene expression datasets collected over a time series across two or more conditions, where the distinct time series have been sampled at the exact same time points.
- pitfalls: All distinct time series experiments must be sampled at the exact same time points ;; Complex models with too many basis functions may get heavily penalized during heteroskedasticity correction, leading to low statistical power ;; Insufficiently complex models may fail to capture expression trajectories, also reducing power ;; Missing values should be handled (e.g., via K-nn imputation) to avoid downstream fitting issues

workflows.name: expressionset_workflow
workflows.intent: Analyze time-course gene expression data starting from an ExpressionSet object.
input: ExpressionSet_object (Bioconductor ExpressionSet containing expression data and metadata with 'Time', 'Sample', and 'Gene Symbol' or 'ORF' columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Build Rnits object and normalize using build.Rnits ;; 2. Impute missing values using getLR ;; 3. Fit B-spline models using fit ;; 4. Extract p-values and statistics using getPval, getStat, getCID, and getFitModel ;; 5. Summarize top genes using summary and topData ;; 6. Plot gene trajectories using plotResults
workflows.code:
rnitsobj = build.Rnits(dat[, sample(ncol(dat))], logscale = TRUE, normmethod = "Between")
lr <- getLR(rnitsobj, impute = TRUE)
rnitsobj <- fit(rnitsobj0, gene.level = TRUE, clusterallsamples = TRUE)
pval <- getPval(rnitsobj)
stat <- getStat(rnitsobj)
table(getCID(rnitsobj))
fitdata <- getFitModel(rnitsobj)
summary(rnitsobj, top = 10)
td <- topData(rnitsobj, fdr = 5)
plotResults(rnitsobj, top = 16)

workflows.name: data_matrix_workflow
workflows.intent: Analyze time-course gene expression data starting from a raw data matrix and separate metadata data frames.
input: probedata_df (data frame containing ProbeID and GeneName columns)
phenodata_df (data frame containing Sample and Time columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Build Rnits object from data matrix and metadata using build.Rnits ;; 2. Fit B-spline models using fit ;; 3. Extract p-values and statistics using getPval, getStat, getCID, and getFitModel ;; 4. Summarize top genes using summary and topData ;; 5. Plot gene trajectories using plotResults
workflows.code:
rnitsobj0 = build.Rnits(datdf, probedata = probedata, phenodata = phenodata, logscale = TRUE, normmethod = 'Between')
rnitsobj <- fit(rnitsobj0, gene.level = TRUE, clusterallsamples = TRUE)
pval <- getPval(rnitsobj)
stat <- getStat(rnitsobj)
table(getCID(rnitsobj))
fitdata <- getFitModel(rnitsobj)
summary(rnitsobj, top = 10)
td <- topData(rnitsobj, fdr = 5)
plotResults(rnitsobj, top = 16)
